If this job description resonates with you, please apply. Frequently cited statistics show that people who identify with historically marginalized groups are likely to apply to jobs only if they meet 100% of the qualifications. About Tailscale 

Tailscale is making safe connection effortless by delivering software that makes it easy to securely interconnect people and their devices, no matter where they are. From hobbyists to multinational corporations, teams of every size use Tailscale each day to protect their networks, share access to internal tools, and more. We're building a future for the Internet that's easy, sensible, and safe, like it used to be. Founded in 2019 and fully distributed, we're backed by Accel, CRV, Insight, Heavybit, and Uncork Capital.
About the Role

Tailscale is looking for a Developer Relations Engineer to own and improve the developer experience across Tailscale’s expanding product portfolio. You’ll help developers understand, adopt, extend, and build with our core VPN/connectivity product, while also shaping how that experience evolves as Tailscale expands into new product areas like secure AI access (Aperture), privileged access management (PAM), and whatever comes next.

You’re a builder, investigator, and storyteller. You write code, chase technical curiosities all the way down, and turn what you learn into things other developers can use like demos, docs, talks, blog posts, sample apps, workshops, videos, tools, and open source contributions. You build things, break things, explain things, and keep going until the thing you’re working on has a name.

You’re comfortable speaking at conferences and just as comfortable digging through an API, a GitHub issue, or a weird networking edge case until it makes sense. You’re probably the kind of person who runs a local AI model in your homelab and can explain exactly why. You ask “why does it work that way?” often, and your instinct is to make the answer clearer, simpler, and better for the next developer.

Requirements 

• Strong software engineering fundamentals, with demonstrated experience building, debugging, and shipping real projects through professional work, open source, self-directed learning, or ambitious personal projects.

• Ability to create clear, useful developer-facing materials, including code samples, demos, tutorials, docs, blog posts, videos, talks, and workshops.

• Deep curiosity about how systems work, especially across networking, infrastructure, security, identity, cloud, open source, AI, or developer tooling.

• A track record of building and explaining technical systems, such as production software, developer tools, infrastructure projects, homelabs, local AI setups, networking experiments, or open source contributions.

• Excellent written, verbal, and visual communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical ideas clearly, creatively, and practically.

• Experience presenting to technical audiences, whether through conferences, meetups, livestreams, workshops, podcasts, videos, or internal engineering forums.

• Comfortable working in public through GitHub issues, pull requests, community forums, social channels, open source projects, and developer feedback loops.

• Strong developer empathy, emotional intelligence, and product sense; you notice friction, understand why it matters, and help translate it into better docs, APIs, examples, workflows, and product experiences.

• Ability to work cross-functionally with engineering, product, marketing, support, community, and other technical stakeholders while operating independently and driving high-impact projects from idea to execution.

• Comfortable managing multiple workstreams, meeting regular publishing, event, or launch deadlines, discussing technical tradeoffs in detail, and traveling for events, conferences, and community moments.

Nice to Have

• Experience with Go, networking, VPNs, WireGuard, identity, access controls, infrastructure automation, or security products.

• Experience building developer education programs, sample apps, workshops, technical video content, or conference talks.

• A visible history of technical writing, talks, demos, open source contributions, or community work.

• Experience with homelabs, self-hosting, local AI models, infrastructure experiments, or other “I wanted to understand how this works, so I built it” projects.

• Familiarity with secure AI access, privileged access management, zero trust, or modern infrastructure security patterns.

• Familiarity with open source contribution workflows and technical collaboration in public.

Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

• Strong software engineering fundamentals, whether gained through formal education, professional experience, open source work, self-directed learning, or building ambitious projects on your own.

• A track record of building and explaining technical systems. This could include production software, developer tools, infrastructure projects, open source contributions, homelab experiments, local AI setups, networking projects, or anything else that shows how you think.

• If your background is less conventional, we still want to hear from you. Bring us your GitHub repos, blog posts, diagrams, configs, talks, demos, lab notes, or the deeply specific story of why your homelab is built the way it is.

• Comfort discussing technical tradeoffs in detail such as explaining what you built, why you built it, what broke, what you learned, and what you would do differently next time.

Company: Altera Health (A Harris Computer Business)

About The Role

We are looking for a Senior Databricks Engineer to join our AI and Automation team. In this role, you will lead the architecture and delivery of scalable data platforms on Databricks, drive engineering best practices, and act as a technical anchor for data pipeline and lakehouse initiatives. You will work closely with AI, automation, and reporting teams to build production-grade data infrastructure that powers healthcare IT operations at scale.

We are looking for someone who is deeply self-sufficient — someone who can independently diagnose, debug, and resolve complex technical issues without hand-holding, and who actively uses AI tooling as a force multiplier to deliver faster and smarter solutions.

Key Responsibilities

Architecture & Technical Leadership

• Own the end-to-end design and architecture of Databricks-based data platforms, including Medallion (Bronze/Silver/Gold) lakehouse patterns
• Define and enforce engineering standards for pipeline development, testing, and deployment across the team
• Lead technical design reviews and contribute to architectural decision-making alongside senior stakeholders
• Evaluate and recommend tools, frameworks, and platform configurations to meet evolving business needs
• Independently investigate and resolve complex platform, pipeline, and performance issues — bringing structured debugging and root cause analysis skills to production incidents

Azure Platform & Cloud Engineering

• Demonstrate deep, hands-on understanding of the Azure ecosystem — not just as a storage layer but as an integrated platform:
• Understand Azure cost governance and resource optimisation at scale
• Architect cross-service solutions that leverage Azure-native capabilities alongside Databricks

Open Source Stack Proficiency

• Bring strong working knowledge of the broader open source data ecosystem:
• Docker — containerization of data applications and pipelines
• Evaluate and adopt open source tooling pragmatically — choosing the right tool without over-engineering
GitHub & Development Practices

• Operate confidently and independently in GitHub:
• Branching strategies (GitFlow, trunk-based development)
• Pull requests, code reviews, and merge conflict resolution
• Repository organisation, tagging, releases, and change management
• Maintain clean, well-documented codebases and enforce code quality standards across the team
• Treat infrastructure and pipeline code with the same rigour as application code
AI-Augmented Engineering

• Actively and fluently use AI tools (GitHub Copilot, Claude, ChatGPT, or equivalent) as a core part of the engineering workflow — not occasionally, but as default practice
• Use AI to accelerate complex problem-solving: debugging cryptic errors, generating boilerplate, refactoring code, writing tests, and exploring unfamiliar APIs
• Leverage LLMs for data pipeline design ideation, documentation generation, and query optimisation
• Comfortable prompting AI effectively to get production-quality outputs and critically evaluating AI-generated code before shipping
• Stay current with AI tooling evolution and bring new productivity patterns to the team

Data Engineering & Pipelines

• Build and optimise complex ETL/ELT pipelines using Apache Spark on Databricks at production scale
• Architect Delta Lake solutions with strong focus on reliability, performance tuning, and cost governance
• Design reusable, modular pipeline frameworks that accelerate team delivery
• Drive CI/CD adoption for data pipelines — automated testing, deployment, and rollback strategies

Analytics & Reporting Enablement

• Collaborate with Power BI reporting teams to deliver well-modelled, governed semantic layers
• Own the design of data models that balance query performance with flexibility for changing requirements
• Act as a technical bridge between engineering and business/reporting consumers

AI & Automation Integration

• Lead data engineering workstreams supporting AI/ML initiatives — feature stores, training pipelines, model serving data flows, and MLflow integration
• Design data feeds and integration layers connecting Databricks outputs with operational tools such as LogicMonitor and ServiceNow ITOM
• Identify and prototype new AI/automation use cases enabled by the data platform

Platform Governance & Reliability

• Own Databricks workspace governance — Unity Catalog, cluster policies, access controls, cost monitoring, and security configurations
• Implement robust data quality frameworks, observability, and alerting for pipeline health
• Ensure compliance with data handling standards relevant to healthcare IT environments
• Mentor mid-level and junior engineers, conducting code reviews and upskilling the team

Required Skills & Experience

• 7+ years of overall data engineering experience, with 4+ years hands-on on Databricks
• Deep expertise in Apache Spark (PySpark and/or Scala) — including performance tuning, partitioning strategies, and cluster optimisation
• Strong command of Delta Lake — ACID transactions, schema evolution, time travel, optimisation techniques
• Advanced SQL and data modelling skills (Kimball, Data Vault, or Lakehouse patterns)
• Deep, proven hands-on experience with Azure — ADLS Gen2, ADF, Azure DevOps, Event Hubs, Key Vault, Monitor, AAD/Entra ID; able to architect cross-service solutions independently
• Strong open source stack knowledge — Kafka, Airflow, dbt, Docker, and related tooling
• GitHub proficiency — branching, PRs, GitHub Actions CI/CD, and repository management
• Strong independent debugging and troubleshooting skills — able to own and resolve complex production issues without escalation
• Demonstrated fluency with AI tools in day-to-day engineering — GitHub Copilot, Claude, or equivalent; uses AI to solve problems, not just for autocomplete
• Excellent communication skills — able to represent technical positions clearly to non-engineering stakeholders

Good to Have

• Experience with Databricks Unity Catalog and enterprise data governance at scale
• Familiarity with Power BI — DirectQuery, composite models, semantic layer design
• Exposure to MLflow, Feature Store, or Model Serving on Databricks
• Knowledge of healthcare data standards (HL7, FHIR, claims/EHR data)
• Familiarity with LogicMonitor telemetry or ServiceNow data models
• Databricks Certified Associate or Professional certification
• Experience with FastAPI/Flask for building lightweight data APIs

Who You Are

• Deeply self-sufficient — you don’t wait for someone to unblock you; you dig in, debug, research, and solve
• You use AI as a natural extension of your engineering toolkit — it makes you faster, not dependent
• Strong instinct for data quality, platform reliability, and operational excellence
• Comfortable driving technical direction in a lean, fast-moving team
• Genuinely curious about AI/automation applications in IT operations and healthcare
• A collaborative mentor who raises the engineering bar across the team
• Treat GitHub as a professional discipline — clean commits, meaningful PRs, documented decisions

f6c879a626bfb00f.description: **About RentOk :** Running a PG or hostel in India means juggling rent, tenants, staff and complaints, mostly through a register, an Excel sheet, WhatsApp or a manager who remembers everything. RentOk brings all of it into one place. More than 25,000 property owners use it, from a 30-bed PG to co-living chains. Their tenants use it for their whole stay, from finding a place to moving out. We want RentOk to be intelligent, proactive and intuitive. It should fill in what it already knows instead of asking, suggest the next step, and do the work for the owner where it is safe. Owners already know the register. RentOk has to be easier than that, as well made as the best apps on their phone, and something people enjoy opening. RentOk is scaling, and we are growing our design team to match. With this role, design will be a team of three: two senior designers and a junior designer, working directly with our CPO. **The role: designer and builder :** Screens are cheap now. Anyone can generate ten in a minute. Choosing the right one, and knowing what to leave out, takes taste and judgment. And a designer no longer has to stop at a picture of the product. You can build the working thing. So we are hiring a product builder as much as a product designer. You will own whole parts of RentOk, like rent collection or a tenant's stay from booking to move-out, from the problem to the product in people's hands. You will know your part better than anyone: who uses it, why each feature exists, and what it does for the business. You will work with business, sales, support, marketing and operations, not only product and engineering, and help decide what we build next. Along the way you will grow our design system and hold the bar in design reviews. **What you will do :** * **Design workflows, not screens. A tenant moving out is one workflow:** the owner works out what the tenant still owes, the manager checks the room, the tenant waits for the deposit, and the parent who paid it wants to know when it comes back. Design all of it. * **Find the problem before you draw.** Visit properties, talk to owners, managers, staff and tenants, ask sharp questions, and turn an unclear problem into a clear direction. * **Make it intuitive for people who live on WhatsApp.** If a caretaker or a first-time owner needs help to use it, simplify until they don't. Write user-first UX copy yourself, in the words they use. * **Have a reason for every decision.** Bring options and a recommendation, and explain what you dropped and why. * **Build the working thing.** Take an idea to a working prototype with AI tools like Claude Code or Cursor, and test it with real users. * **Hand off without gaps.** Work with engineers from the start. Give them the rules, states, permissions, errors and messy real cases, like a partial payment or a tenant who leaves mid-month. If an engineer has to guess, the design is not finished. Then check the build before release, and check after release whether it worked. * **Put love into the details.** People can tell when someone cared. Type, spacing, motion and copy deserve the care the best consumer apps get, most of all where money moves. One wrong amount or a late deposit refund costs the owner the tenant's trust, and costs us the owner's. * **Decide when RentOk acts.** When it reminds, suggests or acts for the owner, when it stays quiet, and what happens when it gets something wrong. **Who we are looking for** * 5+ years designing products, with shipped work and results you can show. * Taste and craft. You know what good looks like, you notice when something is off, and you can say why. * AI is part of how you design. You explore, prototype and test ideas with it. * Strong mobile app design on complex products: B2B, operations, fintech or marketplaces. * Clear communication. You can explain a decision to an engineer, a salesperson and a PG owner, in writing and in person. * Judgment. You hold a point of view, cut steps, and say no with reasons. **A plus if you have** * Shipped your own changes to a live product's code. * Designed products that move money. * Lived in a PG or hostel, or helped run one. **How to apply** Send two or three case studies showing the problem, your decisions and why, and what happened after launch. Include at least one workflow with more than one kind of user, and what you handed to engineers. If you have built something with AI, show us that too. To stand out, download [RentOk on the Play Store](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=net.eazypg.eazypgmanagerhttps://) or open [rentok.com](https://rentok.com/https://), pick one screen you would fix, and show us how.

Take-home assignment (Step 1 of the process)

Please complete a take-home assignment. You are allowed to use LLMs to write code. To ensure that your work will not be used at Fluence, we’ve made it unrelated to healthcare:

Build “LendLoop”: a neighborhood tool-lending board with automated workflows

A simple app where neighbors list tools they are willing to lend, request to borrow from each other, and receive automated notifications and reminders handled by n8n.

Stack

• 

Next.js (App Router)

• 

Clerk for authentication

• 

Convex for data + backend logic

• 

n8n (self-hosted via Docker or n8n Cloud) for workflow automation

• 

TypeScript

Requirements

Public page

• 

The fictional company name is LendLoop.

• 

Short tagline, e.g. “Borrow what you need. Lend what you don’t.”

• 

Show:

• 

A read-only list of available tools (name and category only, no owner details), pulled from Convex.

• 

A “Sign in to lend or borrow” button wired to Clerk.

Authenticated experience

• 

Only signed-in users can:

• 

List a tool with:

• 

name

• 

category (power tools, garden, kitchen, camping, etc.)

• 

condition

• 

short description

• 

Request to borrow a tool for a date range.

• 

Approve or decline requests on their own tools.

• 

Mark a loan as returned.

• 

Show:

• 

All tools with availability status, filterable by category.

• 

“My listings”, “My requests”, and “Incoming requests” views.

• 

Nice, minimal layout.

Roles & rules

• 

Have two roles:

• 

admin:

• 

Can remove any listing, view all loans, and mark a lender as “Trusted Lender”.

• 

user:

• 

Can create, edit, and delete only their own listings, and act only on requests involving their own tools or their own borrowing.

• 

Implement the above role-based access control with best practices, enforced in Convex functions, not only in the UI.

Automation with n8n

• 

Build at least two n8n workflows:

• 

Request notification: when a borrow request is created or changes status, Convex calls an n8n Webhook. The workflow notifies the relevant user (email, Slack, Discord, or a logged mock notification is fine) using only the fields it needs.

• 

Overdue reminders: a scheduled workflow runs daily, fetches overdue loans from a Convex HTTP endpoint, sends a reminder to each borrower, and writes the reminder status back to Convex.

• 

Secure the integration in both directions:

• 

Sign webhook payloads (e.g. HMAC with a shared secret) and verify signatures on the receiving side.

• 

Keep secrets in environment variables and n8n credentials, never in code or exported workflow JSON.

• 

Make write-backs idempotent so retries do not create duplicate records or reminders.

• 

Handle failures with retries and an error workflow (or equivalent) so failed runs are visible and never fail silently.

• 

(Bonus) Show recent automation activity on each loan in the app, e.g. “Reminder sent 2 days ago”.

A GitHub repository with the app source code.

• 

Exported n8n workflow JSON files in the repository.

• 

A README covering local setup (including n8n, e.g. a docker-compose file), environment variables, architecture, and your security and data-minimization decisions.

• 

A short note on what you would change to run this in production.

Security-minded thinking

UX and practicality

Integration design, reliability, and error handling (n8n)

Documentation and reasoning
